content.text: +1 on making those URIs.

Because acl:agent values can be both users or groups, I think it would make sense to have two prefixes. Maybe fcrepo.webac.user.baseUri and fcrepo.webac.group.baseUri? (though maybe there should be an "auth" part of that?). Then, if the value is null, they are treated as strings?
, is this ticket coming out of what Hydra currently does? or from a desire to be better aligned with the WebAC "spec"?
I opened the ticket mostly to sync with the Hydra practice.  But as I was looking at the WebAC wiki page and ontology, I did notice that the acl:agent predicate wants a foaf:Agent, not a literal.
I would be very happy if we could use URIs for agents.
does that preclude the use of literals, which you have built the Fedora specs upon to satisfy the majority of use cases, or can both live in the same implementation?
, I believe support for literals and URIs may be able to coexist... but will defer to
, who had designed it out in the past.
Yes, the implementation that I have in mind for this could easily support literals
and
URIs.
PR:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/pull/58
acl:agent values can now be literals or URIs.
We will need a follow-on ticket to update WebAC documentation – it is necessary to use system properties as baseURIs for users/groups.

I have a potential implementation, allowing the WebAC module to support URIs, but what we really need is a clear use case for this (that is the primary reason it wasn't implemented earlier). If you have a specific use case in mind, could you please add it to
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/Design+-+WebAccessControl+Authorization+Delegate

? In particular, it would be helpful to know if user/group URIs will all have a common baseUri and/or whether the user/group ids will come from the servlet authentication mechanism or whether the value of the effective user will come from an additional header (delegated authN).
Pending community input in the form of use cases.

If the user/group ids are coming from an external system like Hydra or Islandora, then that system can be responsible for making URIs out of them.  If they are email addresses or usernames from a local system, then they can be made into mailto: URIs, or prefixed with a dummy HTTP prefix that identifies them.  If they are from something like OAuth, then they may already be URIs.

Having a defined baseURI seems more useful when servlet auth layer is being used, and the ids provided are email addresses or usernames, which would usually be the case when using common auth modules like LDAP/AD or JDBC.
The
baseURI

mechanism is designed specifically to address the case of servlet auth and mapping usernames/roles to URIs. For delegated (e.g. header-based) authentication, any URI format can be used by a client, and the current PR fully supports that.
: see use case at
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/AIC+Use+Case%3A+Users+and+Groups+as+URIs+in+a+WebAC+Context

Am I reading this correctly that the issue has already been fixed and is just waiting to be merged?  Or is the fact that it is "reopened" mean that there is more to do?  We have a use case for alignment of Fedora's and Hydra's WebAC interpretations if that is something that would be helpful. I might be able to make a case for some developer time in the 2nd half of May if there is a need for additional work.
, This PR:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/pull/58
..adds support for "user" URIs and "group" URIs as long as all of the groups have the same base-URI, and likewise with the users.
Since we do not know if that restriction is valid for actual Fedora installations, this PR has been put on hold.
Is this assumption valid in the case of UMd?
It sounds to me like it would be a valid restriction for our current use case & for the foreseeable future, but possibly not forever.  I'm going to call
's attention to this PR and ask him to review.
This PR came up at [today's Hydra Tech call](
https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/hydra/Hydra+Tech+Call+2016-05-11)
.  Hydra is moving forward with aligning with Fedora's WebAC implementation and has beta releases out now.  Is
's comment enough to move forward with
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/pull/58
, It would be good to hear back from
on this... but in the absence of that, does PR-58 meet the Hydra use cases? If so, that and
's comments probably are enough to move forward.

Thanks for following up on this.  We talked about this question today in a planning meeting.  The consensus was that URIs with all the same base URI would be sufficient for us for now, but it would be good to have

's assessment based on a full review of the PR, if this can wait until next week. Peter has been assigned to a different project for the past two-week sprint, but will be back on Fedora starting on Monday.
, waiting till next week is no problem.  Thanks for following up on this!
, just a heads up, my attention has been called to this and I will be taking a look at it today.
: After taking a look at PR-58 and conferring with

, this appears to meet UMD's use cases. However, I am curious how the use of URIs in the ACLs will affect the agent classes defined using foaf:member on foaf:Group resources. Would the objects of those foaf:member properties also have to change to URIs if you used URIs in your ACLs?
for acl:agentClass constructs (clearly not with bnodes – this is just to express the structure), the users defined with foaf:member would all be URIs:

<> acl:agentClass [
        a foaf:Group ;
        foaf:member <info:umd/user/peter>, <info:umd/user/josh> ]
: Thanks for the clarification. That was what I expected, and it should work for our (UMD's) purposes.
Resolved with
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/commit/08f2df553025464f90384f710222e7c5b4ab74c4
Related clean-up:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/pull/65
Cleanup merged via
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/commit/0d3308c249677af8f25d16968bb306b08909a6be
The integration tests for the WebAC module use literals to identify acl:agents, but they should use URIs.
See
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo-module-auth-webac/blob/master/src/test/resources/acls/01/authorization.ttl#L4
If the WebAC module is actually using URIs already, then the tests should be updated to reflect this.
This is intended to align the Fedora and Hydra WebAC usage.  See
https://github.com/projecthydra/hydra-head/issues/313
for the Hydra Access Controls ticket created for changes there.
